assumptions: HAVID is modeled as a composite high-assurance identifier structure built from cross-endorsed identifier classes that retain their native trust semantics.
Verifier outcomes depend on current resolution, integrity checks, lifecycle state, and local policy rather than on cross-endorsement alone.
The current binding is experimental because the upstream HAVID specification is still evolving.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer delegated authority or action permission from HAVID validation alone.
Do not treat assurance contributed by one identifier class as automatically transferred to another identifier class.
Do not interpret a composite HAVID as valid when one linked identifier is expired, revoked, deactivated, or integrity-unverified.
comparisonNotes: Use this binding when you need to compare composite identifier assurance across trust systems without overstating what cross-endorsement proves.
validationHints: Check that downstream mappings keep identifier class, assurance contribution, lifecycle obligation, and revocation consequence distinct.
Reject any translation that upgrades HAVID validation into blanket trust, governance equivalence, or protocol interoperability.
